title: Is anger (or negative emotion) stored in fat cells? A systematic review of the primary evidence
question: Do primary studies provide evidence that anger, or negative emotion more broadly, is stored, retained, or held within adipocytes (fat cells) or adipose tissue?

pico.population: Humans or animals with adipose tissue
pico.exposure: Anger or other negative emotional states (acute or chronic)
pico.comparator: Neutral emotional state, non-adipose tissue, or unexposed control
pico.outcome: Evidence that the emotional state is stored, retained, encoded, or physically held within adipocytes / adipose tissue (as opposed to merely correlating with fat mass)

inclusion_criteria: Primary research (empirical study with original data), not a review, essay, or opinion piece
Addresses an emotional construct — anger specifically, or a negative-emotion / psychological-stress construct
Examines adipocytes or adipose tissue as the site of interest
Tests or measures a proposed storage, retention, memory, or encoding relationship between the emotional state and the fat tissue (not merely an association with fat quantity)

fields.label: Emotion studied
fields.help: anger, chronic stress, depression, general negative affect, etc.

fields.label: Adipose measure
fields.help: what was measured in fat cells / adipose tissue

fields.label: Proposed mechanism
fields.help: the pathway by which emotion is claimed to reach/persist in fat

supports-literal-storage.label: Supports literal storage of emotion in fat
